(the cause and effect logical fallacy...we see what we want to see and attribute the cause incorrectly as being related to the effect...simply because they sometimes occur together)

A drawing I made this morning...

Is it the FTR that forms after the break of a new high that is important, or is it the decision to engulf that is important?

We focus on the FTR, but the FTR is FO'd all the time to the DP below...there are two scenarios I can think of:

1. The FTR that forms on the break of the high retraces down to the DP...so the DP is a tiny FL after it bounces price.

2. The FTR does not reach the DP to EG, and the DP is an FTR that price can FO to in the future. It is a trap being set.

This is an important concept because we want to predict possible FO, but it is also important when deciding whether an engulf has occured or not. Omid's drawing shows this exact situation...the DP located below the FTR that forms after the break of an important level. The FTB to this zone is a FO unless it breaks the low of the DP

If price visits the DP while forming a FTR, the break of the FTR is an engulf. If price does not reach the DP when the FTR forms, then we have to wait for price to break the low of the DP (not the low of the FTR) before determining if an engulf has happened.

Where I am currently, in terms of my understanding:

Decision points are the areas we look for engulfs/FO's. If the only true engulf is an engulf of trues supply/true demand, we can say:

1. Not every DP/FTR is true supply/demand 2. Every area of TS/TD is a DP/FTR

- Any FTB to a DP is a FO

- ORFL's are our targets (origin FL's up and origin FL's down). This is price's destination.

- Important DP's are like road map that tells us how and when we will reach our destinations. How price reacts to them (FO Vs. EG) determines how and when we will reach our destination: the ORFL.
